speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node along with systemic symptoms like night sweats and weight loss. To help narrow down the cause, could you describe the nature of your abdominal pain and its location? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of any previous cancer diagnoses, and have you noticed any swelling in your abdomen or changes in your urination? I also need to check if you have any pain or swelling in your joints.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of the Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis.
REQUEST TEST: Lymph Node Biopsy.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Cervical Lymph Node Biopsy: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Cervical Lymph Node Biopsy: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index strongly suggest a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Do you have any history of autoimmune disorders or infections like Hepatitis C that might predispose you to this condition?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness and tight clothes suggest significant splenomegaly or ascites, which is common in advanced lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
